chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of rs11629191
predictions: The C and T alleles will not show a reproducible TF-dependent difference in regulatory activity at this site; any disease association could reflect linkage or chance.
falsified_if: A reproducible allele-dependent regulatory effect at this site is demonstrated and depends on a TF binding the variant.

chains.title: Speculative ESR1-dependent regulatory effect

links.claim: As a provisional candidate, ESR1 is hypothesized to bind the T allele more strongly; no occupancy or QBiC-SELEX result is supplied here, so this direction is an untested guess rather than an evidence-based assignment.
The variant is hypothesized to lie in a regulatory element whose activity is altered by ESR1 binding, but element activity is unverified.
The affected target gene is unknown; this hypothesis predicts that the element regulates a gene relevant to breast cancer.
The proposed effect is hypothesized to occur in MCF7 cells, without evidence that ESR1 occupies this site there.
If the regulatory change alters the relevant target gene, it could influence breast cancer risk; the direction of that disease effect is unknown.

predictions: An allele-specific reporter effect should be reduced by ESR1 depletion; the predicted binding direction is greater for T than C.
The target gene and whether increased ESR1 binding activates or represses it cannot be predicted from the information provided.
falsified_if: ESR1 shows no allele-dependent binding or regulatory effect in an informative assay, or ESR1 depletion leaves the allele-specific effect unchanged.

chains.title: Speculative FOXA1-dependent regulatory effect

links.claim: As a provisional alternative, FOXA1 is hypothesized to bind the C allele more strongly; no site occupancy or QBiC-SELEX result is supplied here, so the direction is untested.
The variant is hypothesized to alter FOXA1-dependent activity of a cis-regulatory element, which has not been established.
The target gene is unknown; this hypothesis predicts regulation of a breast-cancer-relevant gene.
The proposed effect is hypothesized to occur in MCF7 cells, but FOXA1 occupancy at the variant is not established.
A FOXA1-dependent change in the unknown target gene could affect breast cancer risk, with no supported prediction for the direction.

predictions: An allele-specific regulatory effect should track FOXA1 binding and be reduced by FOXA1 depletion; the predicted binding direction is greater for C than T.
The predicted FOXA1 dependence distinguishes this candidate from the ESR1 and CTCF candidates.
falsified_if: FOXA1 depletion does not affect an allele-specific regulatory signal, or informative assays show no greater FOXA1 binding to C.

chains.title: Speculative CTCF-dependent regulatory effect

links.claim: As a provisional alternative, CTCF is hypothesized to bind the T allele more strongly; no occupancy or QBiC-SELEX result is supplied here, so this direction is untested.
The variant is hypothesized to alter a CTCF-associated regulatory or chromatin-contact element, but neither such an element nor a contact is established.
The target gene is unknown; this hypothesis predicts that altered CTCF binding changes regulation of a breast-cancer-relevant gene.
The proposed effect is hypothesized to occur in MCF7 cells, without evidence of CTCF occupancy at this site in those cells.
If altered CTCF binding changes target-gene regulation, it could influence breast cancer risk; the direction is unknown.

predictions: An allele-specific regulatory effect should track CTCF binding and be reduced by CTCF depletion; the predicted binding direction is greater for T than C.
A CTCF-dependent effect could involve altered chromatin contacts rather than a simple enhancer-output change.
falsified_if: CTCF depletion does not affect the allele-specific regulatory signal, or informative assays show no greater CTCF binding to T.

matrix.test: Low-cost allele-specific reporter assay in MCF7 cells, comparing C and T constructs with control versus ESR1 depletion

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible C-versus-T reporter difference, or any difference is not ESR1-dependent.
A reproducible C-versus-T reporter difference is reduced by ESR1 depletion; the binding hypothesis predicts stronger ESR1 binding to T.
An allele-specific difference, if present, is not specifically reduced by ESR1 depletion; this test alone does not establish FOXA1 dependence.
An allele-specific difference, if present, is not specifically reduced by ESR1 depletion; this test alone does not establish CTCF dependence.

next_experiment: Run the allele-specific reporter assay in MCF7 cells with and without ESR1 depletion. It is the cheapest proposed test that directly distinguishes the leading ESR1-dependent chain from the null, although a positive result would still require confirmation at the endogenous locus.
